findings.title: A server index this build cannot parse is replaced by the pushing clone's local copy (TM-F29 class, whole index)
findings.status: VULN (reproduced by the differential review on a pristine 0.21.0; fixed: TM-F36)
findings.evidence: read_remote returns (raw, None) when decode fails (:50-52, decode :56-60 swallows everything); push :847-849 does merged = local and upload(expected_raw=raw); upload :176,:180 decodes None and server_copy(current, None) is current; same in Vault__Sync__Tag.py:172-175 and Vault__Sync__Format.py:29-31,64; refresh :280-282 already refuses. check_client (:53) runs after the parse that fails, so min_client cannot keep this client out. Reproduced (scratchpad diffreview/repro_index_overwrite.py): planted a server index with an extra branch of branch_type=archived (rejected by Enum__Branch_Type); decode -> None; bob push -> status pushed; server index bytes changed; the planted branch is gone. Pre-existing since bc0a530 (2026-10-07); the range touched the block in 5c33c19 (N5) and d970599 (TM-F29) without changing this arm. No test plants an unparsable branch entry. Side observation from the first run: a feature name Signatures-Required-v2 is coerced to lowercase by Safe_Str__Feature and written back changed. Re-run against a pristine git archive v0.21.0 extraction: same result. Working-tree edits by another agent at the end of this review (TM-F34, TM-F35) do not touch the remote-is-None arm.
findings.proposed: read_remote distinguishes absent / undecryptable / unparsable and the three writers refuse when raw exists but remote is None (as refresh does); read min_client from the raw dict before the strict parse; carry unknown branch entries like tags. Test: Fixed__Index_Overwrite::test_an_index_this_build_cannot_parse_is_never_overwritten (push, tag create, vault format); TM-F row.

findings.title: A batch reply with no results (empty body, {}, None) counts as a complete success; the local named ref and baseline then move
findings.status: VULN (independent confirmation of AC-H-003; fixed: TM-F33)
findings.evidence: _checked :301-317: result = result or {}; status defaults to ok; failed is empty when results is absent. Vault__API._request :394-399 returns {} for a 2xx with an empty body. Index_Sync.require_written :246-252 has the same shape. After execute_batch returns, Vault__Sync__Push.py:366-367 writes the local named ref and the baseline. Ran: Vault__Batch()._checked({}), _checked(None), _checked({"results": []}) all return without raising. Existing tests (Fixed__Host_Substitution::test_any_op_that_is_not_ok_fails_the_push, Fixed__Index_Overwrite::test_tag_create_fails_when_the_server_does_not_write) cover a present non-ok status only. End-to-end needs an http:// host or a proxy answering 200 with an empty body (A2, TM-R10); A1 gains nothing. Impact: the clone records a head the server does not hold; the next push reports behind/rewound. Duplicate of an uncommitted working-tree fix by another agent of this round (TM-F34, TM-F35 / review AC-H-003: _checked(result, expected), _answered, require_written refusing empty results); kept as independent confirmation, re-run against a pristine v0.21.0 extraction.
findings.proposed: Require len(results) == len(operations) and every op ok in _checked and require_written; a missing results key is "not confirmed". Test with a Vault__API__In_Memory subclass whose batch returns {}.

findings.title: init --restore globs *__uninit.zip but the path guard protects only the exact 0.20.0 spelling (_LEGACY_BACKUP_ZIP)
findings.evidence: CLI__Vault.py:341-346 globs .vault__*.zip and *__uninit.zip, newest mtime wins, prompt names the file. Vault__Path_Guard.py:44-49,102: _LEGACY_BACKUP_ZIP requires [a-z0-9]{4,24}__<timestamp>__[a-z0-9_-]+.zip. Ran: is_protected("evil__uninit.zip") -> False; "My Vault__uninit.zip" -> False; "abcd1234__2026-10-10t00-00-00z__uninit.zip" -> True. So vault data (A5) can plant notes__uninit.zip that clone writes and init --restore offers to restore (the attacker vault key and config). Bounded: the folder already is the attacker vault content, the user must answer yes, the restore allow-list writes store members only (TM-F03), checkout does not preserve mtimes so a real .vault__ backup is newer, and the commit direction is refused by content (Secret_Guard.refuse_bytes). Both halves from 5c33c19.
findings.proposed: One rule for legacy backup names: glob only what _LEGACY_BACKUP_ZIP matches, or protect *__uninit.zip in is_protected. Parametrised negative test on both sides.

findings.title: Hardening: a non-force push with no local named-ref file and a ref on the server would send a plain WRITE
findings.evidence: build_operations :96-105: else WRITE when expected_ref_hash is falsy; Push :201-206 sets it from get_ref_file_hash (None when the local file is missing). v0.20.0 (Vault__Batch.py:96-101, blame 895848f) sent write-if-match without match, which Vault__API__In_Memory.batch :62-67 treats as unconditional (expected is None -> no compare) and TM-F08 notes the live server does too: v0.21.0 made explicit what v0.20.0 already did; not a regression. Reachability: a non-force push pulls first (:165-171) and an accepting pull writes the local named ref (TM-F19); the file is missing only on a first push of a branch (TM-R33) or after a refused pull, which raises earlier. --force is a blind write by contract; --force-with-lease substitutes the server bytes (:937-960).
findings.proposed: Refuse instead of WRITE when not force and not first_push and not absent and expected_ref_hash is None.

findings.title: The two known regression pairs hold: TM-F25->F29 (carried entries round-trip exactly) and TM-F27->F30 (every None from read_regular keeps the committed entry)
findings.evidence: Safe_Str__Index_Entry_Json: regex ^[\x20-\x7E]*\Z matches every ensure_ascii JSON string, trim_whitespace False, strict_validation raises (1 MiB cap is 3e099ee N5); to_json :101-105 re-inserts json.loads(str(c)). read_regular None branches (Vault__Path_Guard.py:181-224) are kept as the committed entry in the scan (Vault__Sync__Base.py:449-456), the tree build (Vault__Sub_Tree.py:48-53) and the sparse commit (Vault__Sync__Commit.py:99-105); other OSErrors raise Vault__Unreadable_File_Error. Runtime evidence for F29 in review/findings/post-patch-validation.md.

findings.title: fetch_missing writes only regex-validated key ids that decrypt under the read key to a public PEM

findings.title: The one secret writer: mkstemp 0600 in the target folder, fsync, os.replace; a link at the path is replaced
findings.evidence: mkstemp O_EXCL 0600, fsync, os.replace; temp unlinked on failure. A link at the folder itself is the documented limit (links above the vault root). Callers: write_private 17, direct 7. Tests: Fixed__Symlinks_And_Local::Test_Fixed__Secret_Files x4, test_Vault__Sync__File_Modes.
